description: Nexus is a solo developer team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We are building OUTPOST: MARS, an interactive space survival and mission-training experience for young explorers. Our goal is to combine game development, space science, NASA open datasets, and engaging storytelling to teach the engineering challenges of sustaining human life on Mars. We value creativity, innovation, scientific accuracy, and practical engineering.
summary:
OUTPOST: MARS is an interactive 2D Mars colony simulation designed to make space science exciting for children aged 7–12.

Players become junior astronauts, explore a Martian outpost and make decisions about power, life support, food production and radiation safety.

Grounded in real NASA datasets, the game transforms complex scientific concepts into engaging, visual, hands-on learning experiences.

Explore Mars. Make decisions. Learn to survive.
details:
🚀 OUTPOST: MARS

Your First Mission. Humanity's Next Frontier.

An Interactive Mars Colony Experience for the Next Generation of Space Explorers.

🔴 Live Game
📁 Git Repo
🎥Demo Video

🌍 The Why — Making Space Science Come Alive

Space exploration is fascinating, but for children, understanding the science behind it can be difficult. Complex concepts like solar storms, radiation exposure, life-support systems and resource management are often presented through textbooks and technical explanations.

We wanted to change that.
What if children didn't just learn about Mars, but actually stepped onto its surface, explored a colony and made decisions like junior astronauts?

🎯 Our Mission

To transform authentic space science into an engaging, visual and interactive learning experience — making the challenges of human exploration on Mars understandable, exciting and accessible to young minds.

🪐 The Experience

Welcome to OUTPOST: MARS, where players become junior astronauts exploring a Martian research outpost.
Through an interactive 2D environment, children discover colony infrastructure, interact with mission facilities and learn by making decisions.

  • 🏠 Habitat — Discover crew survival and life-support systems.
  • ☀️ Solar Farm — Explore energy generation and power management.
  • 🌱 Greenhouse — Understand controlled environments and food production.
  • 🛡️ Storm Shelter — Learn about radiation and astronaut safety.
  • 🛰️ Mission Control — Explore mission operations and scientific discoveries.

Mission Control connects the experience through mission operations and scientific discoveries.


🔬 Learn Through Real NASA Science

This isn't just a Mars-themed game. Its learning experiences are grounded in real scientific resources.

Three interactive science challenges bring space research into gameplay:

⚡ 01 — Solar Storm Alert

Analyze a historical X5.8 solar flare from NASA DONKI and make decisions balancing crew protection and colony power.

☢️ 02 — Radiation Detective

Compare real radiation measurements from NASA's Curiosity rover and ISS DOSIS 3D telemetry. Discover why radiation environments differ between Mars and Earth orbit.

📦 03 — The 30-Day Supply Problem


Use NASA life-support planning standards to calculate the oxygen and water needed to sustain a crew on a 30-day mission.
Our approach: Real scientific observations provide the foundation; simplified simulations make the concepts accessible to children.

🛰️ Powered by NASA Resources

Our experience incorporates:

  • NASA DONKI — Historical solar flare observations.
  • NASA PDS / Curiosity RAD — Martian surface radiation measurements.
  • NASA OSDR / RadLab — ISS radiation telemetry.
  • NASA BVAD 2022 — Exploration life-support planning standards.
  • NASA OSDR Space Biology — Research references on spaceflight biology.

Scientific datasets are bundled as offline snapshots, allowing the experience to run without depending on live API connections.

🛠️ Technology Behind the Mission

Built with a lightweight, web-based game architecture:

Phaser 3.90 - 2D game engine
TypeScript - Game logic and simulation
Vite - Development and production builds
HTML & CSS - Interface and responsive presentation
JSON - Offline NASA scientific data snapshots
Local Storage - Saving player progress


🌟 The Impact We Want to Create

We don't want children to simply memorize facts about Mars.
We want them to understand why astronauts need radiation protection, why water and oxygen must be carefully planned, and how space weather can affect a mission.

By combining exploration, visual storytelling and decision-based learning, OUTPOST: MARS aims to spark curiosity about science, engineering and humanity's future beyond Earth.

Because today's curious children could become tomorrow's space explorers.
